stories.title: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya
summary: The highest United Nations court ruled on Thursday that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Rohingya Muslim minority population in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.
The decision by the International Court of Justice, or World Court, is expected to have repercussions far beyond Myanmar, including for South Africa’s 2023 case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza.

A panel of 15 judges said “the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar’s actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part of the protected group namely the Rohingya population in Northern Rakhine state,” meeting the legal threshold for genocide.

stories.title: Pakistan inch closer to victory in second Test despite Sri Lanka fightback
summary: Sri Lanka fought their way into an 82-run lead but Pakistan remained firmly in control of the second Test after reducing the visitors to 309-9 at stumps on the third day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Milan Rathnayake led the resistance with an unbeaten 60, while Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha also scored half-centuries to help Sri Lanka recover from a precarious position.
Sri Lanka resumed their second innings at 74-3, still trailing Pakistan by 153 runs after being bowled out for 98 in their first innings.

stories.title: China and Russia release 'peace declaration' after Trump, Xi, Putin meeting
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin agreed on a “peace declaration” at their unprecedented three-way meeting on Thursday in which they reaffirmed that a nuclear war should never be fought, China and Russia said.
Its not an easy thing to do give them up, Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of their meeting.

Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China.

stories.title: PM credits economic successes to 'productive partnership' between political, military leadership
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said Pakistan’s economic achievements were the product of a “productive partnership between the military and the political hierarchy”.
He was addressing a ceremony organised by the American Business Council of Pakistan.

During his address, the premier acknowledged that the members of the American Business Council of Pakistan had contributed “immensely” in promoting Pakistan’s economic interests. “I have no doubt that you are great ambassadors for Pakistan,” he said.

stories.title: Airspace ban on Indian aircraft extended till Dec 23
summary: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft until Dec 23, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA).

The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Nov 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said.

On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass announced a series of measures, including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country.

stories.title: DPM Dar, Asean secretary general discuss opportunities to expand trade, investment with bloc's member states: FO
summary: DPM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with the Asean Secretariat and member states to advance the partnership.
Pakistan has been an Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 1993, and a member of the Asean Regional Forum since 2004, FO added.
Last year, seven Asean member countries held a joint meeting with Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh to explore new avenues of investment and economic cooperation with Pakistan.

stories.title: Formation of electoral reforms committee delayed because opposition not finalising nominees: minister
summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Thursday said the formation of the Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) had been delayed because the opposition had yet to submit its nominees.

However, PTI believes that, as in 2017, when an electoral reform process was undertaken, the government and opposition should have equal representation in the PCER to prevent one-sided decision-making.

Earlier this month, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, formally appr­oached its allies to join the proposed PCER.

stories.title: Navy’s combat capabilities significantly enhanced across all operational domains: Admiral Ashraf
summary: Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Thursday said the Pakistan Navy has significantly enhanced its combat capabilities across all operational domains.

The naval chief further said that the navy’s combat capabilities “have recently undergone significant enhancement and transformation across all operational domains aligned with contemporary and future warfare demands”.

The naval chief described the air force and navy as “brothers in arms”, with the “maritime domain as our shared operational space”. “It is here we exercise together and shall fight alongside each other to defend our motherland.

In January, a passenger vehicle overturned on the coastal highway in Ormara, killing 10 people and leaving more than 30 others injured.

stories.title: Islam forecast to exceed Christianity as world's biggest religion by middle of next decade
summary: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s biggest religion by the middle of the next decade, the Pew Research Centre projected on Wednesday.

While Christianity has ranked as humanity’s largest religion for centuries, the global Muslim population has grown much faster and is forecast to reach 2.57 billion by 2035, compared with a projected tally of 2.52bn Christians in that year, the Pew study found.

The Pew study also concluded that Pakistan’s Muslim population was expected to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461m in 2070. “The country will rise from having the second-largest Muslim population to the world’s largest,” it said.

stories.title: Two PTI-affiliated Pakistanis detained in UAE over 'state security' cases, LHC told
summary: LAHORE: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) has informed the Lahore High Court (LHC) that two Pakistani citizens affiliated with the PTI and detained at Abu Dhabi’s Al-Wathba Jail are being held in connection with cases relating to “state security”.
The ministry said it had received an email from the family on Oct 1 requesting the submission of a mercy petition to the UAE’s Royal Court through MoFA.
The ministry said a mercy petition was emailed to MoFA on Oct 1 for submission to the UAE’s Royal Court, but was subsequently withdrawn.

stories.title: CDF Munir briefed on ongoing operations during Balochistan visit: ISPR

Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37 per cent, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57pc, and injuries decreasing by 71pc compared to September, the report said.

China has the world’s fastest-growing nuclear arsenal and has repeatedly expressed no interest in joining US-Russian arms control arrangements until it reaches a position of parity.

The three presidents can discuss what is known as horizontal proliferation, the spread of nuclear weapons to others, but the reality is that Russia and China have not reined in North Korea’s growing program.

stories.title: Trump says US will 'see what happens' in conflict with Iran after January 1
summary: US President Donald Trump said in comments broadcast on Thursday that the United States would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining what the significance of that date might be.
Trump made the comments during an interview in which he was asked about a report carried by CNN this week that Iran was planning to detonate a "dirty bomb" in Washington.
Destroying Iran's nuclear programme was one of Trump's main justifications when he launched strikes against Iran in February alongside Israel.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz credits civil-military cooperation for Pakistan's economic stability
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday credited cooperation between the civilian government and military leadership for Pakistan's economic progress, saying stronger coordination could help transform the country's economy and accelerate growth across key sectors.
Addressing a ceremony hosted by the American Business Council, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says the government is making every effort to attract maximum foreign investment to Pakistan.
The prime minister called for closer cooperation between the government and private sector, saying Pakistan needed to learn from past mistakes and move forward through collective efforts.

The MQM-P chief also said his party had planned a demonstration in support of new provinces for November 29, but postponed it due to security concerns.

stories.title: At least 10 killed, 27 injured as coach collides with LPG bowser in Gwadar
summary: QUETTA: At least 10 people, including a woman and three children, were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger coach collided with a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) bowser on the Makran Coastal Highway near Taji checkpost in Balochistan on Thursday.
The passenger coach was travelling from Turbat to Karachi when it collided with the bowser near Basol in the Ormara area of Gwadar district, causing both vehicles to burst into flames.
In August, six people were burnt to death in a collision near Ormara, while in January, nine passengers were killed and 36 injured when a passenger coach overturned on the same highway.

stories.title: Anthropic to begin trading after record-breaking market debut tops SpaceX record
summary: Its listing will give ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant when it begins trading under the ticker “ANT.” The offering breaks the record $75 billion that Elon Musk’s SpaceX raised in June at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.
SpaceX ultimately raised $86 billion after the banks underwriting the IPO exercised options to buy additional shares.
Anthropic’s IPO filing gives extensive detail to the risks of the technology, reflecting the company’s focus on safety even as it builds ever more powerful models.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar sign security cooperation agreement, action plan to curb drug trafficking
summary: Pakistan and Qatar on Thursday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on security cooperation between Qatar's Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya) and Pakistan's Federal Constabulary, along with an action plan to prevent drug trafficking, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif witnessed the signing ceremony during a meeting with Qatar's Interior Minister and Commander of the Internal Security Force, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, in Islamabad.
According to the PMO, Sheikh Khalifa thanked Pakistan for its hospitality and conveyed the Emir of Qatar's greetings and best wishes to the prime minister.

stories.title: Two sentenced to life imprisonment in rape case in Karachi
summary: Additional District and Sessions Judge (South) Abdul Zahoor Chandio found the victim’s mother, Suraiya, her stepfather, Amjad Ali, and his accomplice Zafar Iqbal, guilty and sentenced the two men to life imprisonment and the woman to three-year in prison.
The victim further alleged that her mother had taken Rs16,000 from accused Iqbal, who was an acquaintance of her stepfather, and claimed that he had also sexually assaulted her.

The court rejected the defence’s pleas and noted that the DNA report provides particularly strong corroboration against accused Zafar while the case against accused Amjad rests upon the victim’s direct account of repeated assaults, supported by the medical findings.

stories.title: Newborn ‘bitten by animals’ dies in Sukkur's Pano Aqil hospital incubator
summary: SUKKUR: A newborn died at a private hospital in Pano Aqil after allegedly being bitten by cats or other animals in an incubator room, prompting allegations of negligence against the facility.
The newborn, who had breathing difficulties, was placed in an incubator on the staff’s advice, in a room to which animals allegedly had access.
The father then spoke to the media about the hospital’s alleged negligence.

stories.title: PSX rises around 700 points in mid-day trade
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s benchmark KSE-100 Index advanced 696.23 points, or 0.39 per cent, to 176,990.56 by mid-day on Thursday, recovering part of the previous session’s losses.

Early trade saw the Index climb close to 1,200 points as buying interest returned across several heavyweight sectors, including cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration, oil marketing companies, power generation and refineries.
Market participants noted selective accumulation after the previous day’s decline, with the Index holding above its previous close through the first half of the session.

stories.title: Punjab CM approves panchayat system to resolve disputes
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Wednesday gave approval to the establishment of a “panchayat system” aimed at resolving local disputes through mediation.
The decision was taken at a meeting presided over by the chief minister where officials gave a briefing on the proposed framework.

She observed that courts should not necessarily be the first forum for resolving every disagreement, adding that dialogue and the wisdom of respected community members could help settle many disputes.

stories.title: Large amount of suspected donkey meat seized in Islamabad
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad Food Authority (IFA), along with the capital police, recovered 800 kilogrammes of meat believed to be of different animals, including donkeys, during a raid on a house in a rural area of Islamabad.
Documents belonging to a Chinese national were found at the premises where the meat was being processed.

According to the FIR, acting on information received from the IFA, a team from the Islamabad Wildlife Management Board (IWMB) visited the house where wild animals were reportedly being kept in illegal captivity.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy enhances combat capabilities to meet demands of future warfare: Naval chief
summary: Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Thursday said the Pakistan Navy's combat capabilities had undergone significant enhancement and transformation across all operational domains to meet the demands of contemporary and future warfare.

Referring to the May 2025 conflict with India, Admiral Ashraf said Pakistan's armed forces had demonstrated their ability to deter aggression, adding that the adversary had “learned the lesson” and that it would be “unwise to need a second”.
The naval chief said the Pakistan Navy had successfully deterred the Indian Navy from engaging in hostilities at sea during Marka-e-Haq, keeping it at bay throughout the conflict.

stories.title: Jepchirchir gets 3-year ban for doping
summary: Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday, in the latest blow to the reputation of Kenyan athletics.
They join more than 140 Kenyan athletes, including current women's marathon world record-holder Ruth Chepngetich, who have been suspended or banned by the AIU since 2017.
Kenya hosted a three-day visit from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) last month, the body's chief Witold Banka telling the country that it had to strive for zero tolerance on doping.

stories.title: F1 hits Vegas with titles settled, podiums up for grabs
summary: While Antonelli -- confirmed as the youngest world champion in F1 history -- can soak up the adulation, his teammate George Russell will jostle for points with multiple-time world champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, in the 21st of 23 rounds this season.
Russell sits third in the rankings on 262 points, trailing Red Bull's Verstappen -- who is enjoying a stellar end to the season -- by 17, and leading Ferrari's Hamilton by a single point.
Verstappen -- who won last year's Las Vegas race -- and Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar are ending the season in strong form.

stories.title: Eisenkot bloc moves to reverse Netanyahu legacy under new speaker
summary: In the vote for parliament speaker late on Tuesday, 66 lawmakers out of 120 voted in favour of Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu.
With Kahana at the helm, Eisenkot’s camp has an opportunity to deal blows to Netanyahu’s legislative agenda even before a possible government is formed.
The Knesset is due to hold preliminary votes on bills designed to reverse Netanyahu-era legislation which increased political influence over the judiciary and the media.
